questions.title: Total number of spinal nerve pairs
questions.question: The number of spinal nerves is:

explanations.A: Correct. The spinal cord gives rise to 31 pairs of spinal nerves, one per spinal cord segment: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 1 coccygeal. Each nerve forms from the union of a dorsal (sensory) root and a ventral (motor) root, making every spinal nerve mixed. This count is distinct from the 33 vertebrae (the sacral vertebrae fuse into one sacrum and there is a single coccyx) and from the 12 pairs of cranial nerves, which arise from the brain rather than the cord.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 33 is the vertebral count, not the spinal nerve count -- sacral fusion and the single coccyx mean fewer nerve pairs than vertebrae.
explanations.C: Incorrect. 12 is the number of cranial nerve pairs, which arise from the brain, not the spinal nerve count.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 14 does not correspond to any standard count in this system; it is a plausible-looking distractor with no anatomical basis here.

questions.subject: neuro
questions.learning_objective: State that there are 31 pairs of spinal nerves, distinguishing this from the vertebral and cranial nerve counts.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: 31 pairs" (QUIZ21&22 Q1).

questions.title: Structural and functional unit of the nervous system
questions.question: The structural and functional units of the nervous system are:

explanations.A: Correct. The neuron is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system: every task the nervous system performs is carried out by neurons acting individually or in circuits. A neuron has a cell body and two kinds of processes, dendrites and an axon. Glial cells support and insulate neurons but do not themselves generate or conduct nerve impulses, so they are not the functional unit.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Axons are a neuron's own process, not a complete functional unit in themselves.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Glial cells support neurons (insulation, metabolic support) but do not generate or conduct impulses.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Dendrites, like axons, are a neuron's process, not a complete functional unit.

questions.subject: neuro
questions.learning_objective: Identify the neuron as the structural and functional unit of the nervous system, distinguishing it from its own processes and from glial cells.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Neurons" (QUIZ21&22 Q2).

questions.title: Subdivisions of the central nervous system
questions.question: The CNS is subdivided into:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The brainstem and cerebrum are both parts of the brain, not co-equal partners with the spinal cord in this division.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The brainstem is a part of the brain, not a separate CNS subdivision alongside the spinal cord.
explanations.C: Correct. The nervous system divides into the CNS and the peripheral nervous system (PNS); the CNS itself is subdivided into the brain, housed in the cranial cavity, and the spinal cord, housed in the vertebral canal and continuous with the brain through the foramen magnum. The PNS -- cranial and spinal nerves and their ganglia -- lies outside this division. This brain/spinal cord split is the standard first-level anatomical subdivision of the CNS taught at this stage.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The cerebrum is only one part of the brain, not a co-equal CNS subdivision alongside the brain as a whole.

questions.subject: neuro
questions.learning_objective: State that the CNS is subdivided into the brain and the spinal cord.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Brain and spinal cord" (QUIZ21&22 Q3).

questions.title: Composition of gray matter
questions.question: Gray matter consists of:

options.A: Collections of neuronal axons outside the CNS
options.B: Bodies of nerve cells embedded in neuroglia

explanations.A: Incorrect. Collections of axons outside the CNS describe a peripheral nerve, not gray matter.
explanations.B: Correct. Gray matter is composed of the bodies (perikarya) of nerve cells, together with dendrites, synapses and unmyelinated fibres, embedded in a supporting network of neuroglia. This is what gives gray matter its darker appearance relative to white matter, which is instead composed of myelinated axons collected into tracts. In the spinal cord gray matter occupies the central, butterfly-shaped core; in the cerebrum and cerebellum it forms the outer cortex.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Nerve fibers (axons) embedded in neuroglia describes white matter, not gray matter.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Axons embedded in neuroglia again describes white matter, not the cell-body composition of gray matter.

questions.subject: neuro
questions.learning_objective: State that gray matter is composed of nerve cell bodies embedded in neuroglia, distinguishing it from white matter.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Bodies of nerve cells embeded in neuroglia" (QUIZ21&22 Q4).

questions.title: Nerve fibres carrying impulses from the CNS to the periphery
questions.question: The nerves that carry impulses from the brain to the body are:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Afferent (sensory) fibres carry impulses from the periphery toward the CNS -- the opposite direction.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A receptor is a sensory structure, not a nerve fibre class carrying impulses away from the CNS.
explanations.C: Correct. Efferent (motor) nerves carry impulses away from the central nervous system out to effector organs such as muscles and glands. This is the opposite direction to afferent (sensory) nerves, which carry impulses from peripheral receptors toward the CNS. Somatic efferent fibres innervate skeletal muscle and autonomic efferent fibres innervate smooth muscle, cardiac muscle and glands, but both are efferent because both conduct away from the CNS.
explanations.D: Incorrect. "Somatic" describes a category of fibre (supplying skin/skeletal muscle) rather than the direction of conduction, and does not by itself specify carrying impulses from the CNS outward.

questions.subject: neuro
questions.learning_objective: State that efferent nerves carry impulses from the CNS to the periphery.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Efferent" (QUIZ21&22 Q5).

questions.title: Surface epithelial cells rest on the basement membrane
questions.question: Epithelial cells rest directly on which structure?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Epithelium is separated from the connective tissue proper by the basement membrane; it does not rest directly on connective tissue with nothing between.
explanations.B: Correct. Every epithelium rests on a basement membrane, and having one is what distinguishes epithelium from the tissues around it -- epithelial cells are crowded with minimal intercellular space and avascular, fed by diffusion from the connective tissue beneath through this basement membrane. On light microscopy the basement membrane is an amorphous layer staining red with PAS. It may be clear and thick, as in skin, or non-clear and thin, as in transitional epithelium.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Epithelium does not rest directly on cartilage; cartilage is itself covered by a connective-tissue perichondrium in most sites.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Epithelium does not rest directly on bone; where epithelium overlies bone (e.g. periosteum-covered surfaces), connective tissue and a basement membrane still intervene.

questions.title: General character of epithelial tissue: cell crowding
questions.question: Epithelial tissues are characterised by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Epithelium has minimal, not abundant, extracellular matrix between its cells -- that description fits connective tissue instead.
explanations.B: Correct. Epithelial tissue's cells are crowded with minimal intercellular space, one of its defining general characters alongside resting on a basement membrane and being avascular. This close aggregation, joined by intercellular junctions, is what lets epithelium form continuous covering or lining sheets. It also has a high power of regeneration and may be ectodermal, mesodermal or endodermal in origin.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Epithelium is avascular -- blood vessels cannot penetrate between epithelial cells, so it is fed by diffusion from the connective tissue beneath instead.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Widely separated cells is the opposite of epithelium's actual close cellular packing.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: State that epithelial tissue is characterised by closely aggregated cells with minimal extracellular matrix.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Closely aggregated cells" (Quiz 23 Q2). Concept reused from docs/Kasr-Source-Imports/concept/101-ISK-mcq-concepts.md (CON-FND-49350AB867CB5A); overlay in docs/Assiut-Source-Imports/pending-live/AUN-PMS-102-histology-overlay.md.

questions.title: Basement membrane function: molecular filtering
questions.question: The functions of the basement membrane include which of the following?

explanations.A: Correct. The basement membrane's functions are support, attachment, and control of the passage of molecules -- in the kidney glomerulus and the lung alveolus this control of passage is specifically filtration and gas exchange. Electron microscopically it is two layers, the epithelium's own basal lamina (type IV collagen and glycoproteins) and the connective tissue's reticular lamina (type III collagen), with hemidesmosomes fixing the epithelium to it. Molecular filtering is therefore a genuine, well-established basement membrane function, not a property of the epithelial cells themselves.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Contractility is a property of myo-epithelial cells, not the basement membrane itself.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Modification of secreted protein is a function of the Golgi apparatus within a cell, not the basement membrane.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Active ion transport is a function of specialised transporting epithelial cells, not the basement membrane as a structure.

questions.learning_objective: State that molecular filtering is a function of the basement membrane.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Molecular filtering" (Quiz 23 Q3). Concept reused from docs/Kasr-Source-Imports/concept/101-ISK-mcq-concepts.md (CON-FND-47743DDD3ED7A0); overlay in docs/Assiut-Source-Imports/pending-live/AUN-PMS-102-histology-overlay.md.

questions.title: Basement membrane serves multiple roles at once
questions.question: The basement membrane serves:

options.B: To connect the epithelial layers with the underlying tissues
options.C: As a diffusion or filtration barrier

explanations.A: Correct. The basement membrane's functions are support, attachment (connecting epithelium to underlying tissue), and control of the passage of molecules, acting as a diffusion or filtration barrier where relevant (e.g. glomerulus, alveolus). Because it performs all three of these roles simultaneously, rather than only one, "all of the above" is the accurate summary answer among options that each name only one function. Electron microscopically these functions map onto its two-layer structure (basal lamina plus reticular lamina), with hemidesmosomes providing the physical attachment.
explanations.B: Incorrect on its own -- attachment is one genuine function, but the basement membrane also supports and filters, so this option alone is incomplete.
explanations.C: Incorrect on its own -- diffusion/filtration barrier is one genuine function, but the basement membrane also attaches and supports, so this option alone is incomplete.
explanations.D: Incorrect on its own -- support is one genuine function, but the basement membrane also attaches and filters, so this option alone is incomplete.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: State that the basement membrane simultaneously supports, attaches and filters -- not just one of these roles.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: All of the above" (Quiz 23 Q4). Concept reused from docs/Kasr-Source-Imports/concept/101-ISK-mcq-concepts.md (CON-FND-47743DDD3ED7A0); overlay in docs/Assiut-Source-Imports/pending-live/AUN-PMS-102-histology-overlay.md.

questions.title: Stain demonstrating the basement membrane
questions.question: The basement membrane can be stained with:

explanations.A: Correct. Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) is a histochemical reaction for carbohydrate, and it stains what it finds magenta-red: the glycogen of liver and muscle cells, the mucus of goblet cells, the sugar-rich reticular fibre collagen, the basement membrane, and the cell coat glycocalyx. Best's carmine is the older stain for the same carbohydrate target. A PAS-positive result therefore names a class of molecule (carbohydrate) rather than one single structure, but the basement membrane is reliably among the structures it reddens.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Iron hematoxylin demonstrates nuclei and certain fibres/striations, not carbohydrate-rich structures like the basement membrane specifically.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Orcein stains elastic fibres, not the carbohydrate-based basement membrane.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sudan black demonstrates lipid, not the carbohydrate component of the basement membrane.

questions.learning_objective: State that the basement membrane is demonstrated by the PAS reaction.

questions.title: Junction responsible for strong intercellular adhesion
questions.question: Strong adhesion between cells needs:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The gap junction is a communicating junction that lets ions and small molecules pass between cells; it does not provide strong mechanical adhesion.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The zonula adherens is an adhering belt that anchors actin filaments, providing lateral adhesion, but it is not the strongest of the junctions.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The tight (occluding) junction seals the intercellular space to restrict passage of substances; sealing, not maximal mechanical strength, is its defining role.
explanations.D: Correct. The desmosome (macula adherens) does not encircle the cell like a belt -- it is scattered as circular disc-shaped spots, each with a thickened cytoplasmic attachment plaque into which bundles of intermediate filaments (tonofilaments) are anchored. It is the strongest of the junctions, which is why it is abundant between the cells of stratified squamous epithelium, where the surface is subjected to friction. This makes desmosomes the correct answer whenever a question asks specifically for strong intercellular adhesion.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: Identify desmosomes as the junction providing the strongest intercellular adhesion.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Desmosomes" (Quiz 24 Q1). Concept reused from docs/Kasr-Source-Imports/concept/101-ISK-mcq-concepts.md (CON-FND-59E3FDA20F54AD); overlay in docs/Assiut-Source-Imports/pending-live/AUN-PMS-102-histology-overlay.md.

questions.title: Junction mediating intercellular ionic exchange
questions.question: Intercellular ionic exchange is achieved by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The zonula adherens anchors actin filaments for lateral adhesion; the intercellular space it leaves is wide, and nothing passes through it between cells.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The macula adherens (desmosome) anchors intermediate filaments for strong spot adhesion; it does not provide a channel for ionic exchange.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The zonula occludens seals the intercellular space to restrict passage; sealing is the opposite of allowing ionic exchange.
explanations.D: Correct. The gap junction, or nexus, is a communicating junction; the narrow gap between the two membranes is bridged by channels, each formed of six symmetrical transmembrane protein subunits, through which ions and small molecules pass directly from the interior of one cell to the interior of the next. Between muscle cells the same channels carry electrical impulses. It is the only one of the lateral junctions through which anything actually passes, and it is not part of the junctional complex.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: Identify the gap junction as the structure mediating intercellular ionic exchange.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Gap junction" (Quiz 24 Q2). questions.title: Junction responsible for intercellular sealing
questions.question: Intercellular sealing is achieved by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Desmosomes provide strong spot adhesion via intermediate filaments; they do not seal the intercellular space.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Macula adherens is another name for the desmosome, providing adhesion, not sealing.
explanations.C: Correct. The tight, or occluding, junction (zonula occludens) is the most apical of the lateral junctions. The two adjacent plasma membranes fuse at points through transmembrane proteins contributed by each cell, obliterating the intercellular space at those points, and the junction completely encircles the apex of the cell like a belt. Its effect is to restrict the passage of substances between adjacent cells, making the epithelium a barrier rather than a sieve and forcing anything crossing it to pass through the cells rather than between them.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The zonula adherens is an adhering belt (anchoring actin) that leaves a wide intercellular space; it holds cells together but does not seal the space between them.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: Identify the zonula occludens (tight junction) as the structure sealing the intercellular space.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Zonula occludens" (Quiz 24 Q3). Concept reused from docs/Kasr-Source-Imports/concept/101-ISK-mcq-concepts.md (CON-FND-2EAD7BC676C215); overlay in docs/Assiut-Source-Imports/pending-live/AUN-PMS-102-histology-overlay.md.

questions.title: Chamber forming the base of the heart
questions.question: The base of the heart is formed mainly by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The right atrium contributes only a smaller part of the base; it does not form it mainly.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The right ventricle forms part of the anterior (sternocostal) surface of the heart, not the base.
explanations.C: Correct. The heart is a pyramid-shaped organ with an apex, pointing anteroinferiorly and to the left, and a base, which faces posteriorly. The base of the heart is formed mainly by the left atrium, with a smaller contribution from the right atrium, and it receives the four pulmonary veins and lies against the oesophagus and descending aorta. This is distinct from the apex, formed by the left ventricle.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The left ventricle forms the apex of the heart, not the base.

questions.title: Arterioles as the final distributing vessels
questions.question: Regarding the blood vessels, the correct statement is:

options.A: Small veins drain into venules that open into larger veins
options.B: The largest veins, such as the SVC and IVC, carry blood from the heart
options.C: The final distributing vessels, arterioles, deliver oxygenated blood to capillaries
options.D: The interchange of oxygen and waste products with the extracellular fluid occurs through venules

explanations.A: Incorrect. The venous drainage direction is reversed here -- venules drain capillaries into small veins, which then join progressively larger veins, not the stated order.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The SVC and IVC are the largest veins and carry blood toward the heart (into the right atrium), not away from it.
explanations.C: Correct. Arterioles, the smallest branches of the arterial tree, act as the final distributing vessels, regulating flow into the capillary beds and delivering oxygenated blood to them. This is distinct from venules, which drain deoxygenated blood and waste away from capillaries, and from the largest veins (SVC, IVC), which carry blood toward the heart rather than distributing it outward. The interchange of oxygen and waste with the extracellular fluid occurs at the capillary bed itself, between the arteriole and venule ends.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Exchange with the extracellular fluid occurs at the capillary bed, not through the venules, which simply drain the capillaries afterward.

questions.subject: cvs
questions.module_subject: AUN-PMS-102 > Cardiovascular Anatomy > Heart and Great Vessels
questions.learning_objective: Identify arterioles as the final distributing vessels delivering oxygenated blood to capillaries.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: The final distributing vessels, arterioles, deliver oxygenated blood to capillaries" (QUIZ 25 Q2).

questions.title: Example of an anatomic end artery
questions.question: One of these arteries is an example of an anatomic end artery:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The femoral artery takes part in a rich collateral anastomotic network around the lower limb and is not a true end artery.
explanations.B: Correct. An anatomic (true) end artery supplies a region of tissue with no effective anastomosis to a neighbouring artery's territory, so its occlusion causes ischaemia or infarction of the tissue it supplies. The pulmonary artery and its branches are a classic teaching example of anatomic end arteries. This is in contrast to the femoral, common carotid and lingual arteries, which all take part in rich collateral anastomotic networks and are not end arteries in this strict sense.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The common carotid artery's branches anastomose extensively (e.g. via the circle of Willis and external carotid collaterals) and it is not a true end artery.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The lingual artery anastomoses with its contralateral partner and neighbouring vessels in the tongue and floor of the mouth and is not a true end artery.

questions.subject: cvs
questions.module_subject: AUN-PMS-102 > Cardiovascular Anatomy > Heart and Great Vessels
questions.learning_objective: Identify the pulmonary artery as a classic example of an anatomic end artery.

questions.title: Distinguishing veins from arteries at the bedside
questions.question: The difference between arteries and veins is:

options.A: Veins do not pulsate and do not squirt or spurt blood when severed
options.B: The walls of arteries are thinner than those of veins
options.C: Veins tend to be single only
options.D: Medium arteries in the limbs have valves that permit blood flow in one direction

explanations.A: Correct. Arteries carry blood under pulsatile pressure generated by the heartbeat, so a severed artery pulsates and blood spurts from it; veins carry blood under low, non-pulsatile pressure, so a severed vein neither pulsates nor spurts blood. This bedside distinction is a practical way to identify arterial versus venous bleeding. Arterial walls are also thicker and more muscular than venous walls, not the reverse.
explanations.B: Incorrect. This reverses the true relationship -- arterial walls are thicker than venous walls, not thinner.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Veins are frequently paired (venae comitantes accompany many arteries) rather than uniformly single.
explanations.D: Incorrect. It is specifically the medium and large veins of the limbs, not arteries, that contain valves permitting one-directional flow toward the heart.

questions.module_subject: AUN-PMS-102 > Cardiovascular Anatomy > Heart and Great Vessels

questions.title: Correct statement about the lymphatic system
questions.question: Regarding the lymphatic system, the correct statement is:

options.A: Lymphoid tissue is not found in the walls of the digestive tract
options.B: Lymph is usually clear and yellow in colour and is similar in composition to blood plasma
options.C: Lymphatic vessels are found in all tissues and organs of the body
options.D: Lymph vessels have a beaded appearance

explanations.A: Incorrect. Lymphoid tissue is in fact present in the walls of the digestive tract (e.g. Peyer's patches of the ileum), so this statement is false, not correct.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Lymph is typically described as clear/colourless to pale, and while related to plasma it is not simply "similar in composition to blood plasma" as a precise, examinable statement.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Lymphatic vessels are absent from some tissues, such as avascular tissues (e.g. cartilage) and the central nervous system parenchyma, so "all tissues and organs" overstates their distribution.
explanations.D: Correct. Lymphatic vessels have a characteristic beaded, or nodular, appearance along their length, produced by the numerous valves within them that keep lymph flowing in one direction toward the venous system. This valve-driven beading is a reliable identifying feature of lymphatics on gross or microscopic inspection. It distinguishes them from blood vessels, which do not show this same regular nodularity.

questions.subject: cvs
questions.learning_objective: State that lymphatic vessels have a beaded appearance due to their numerous valves.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Lymph vessels have a beaded appearance" (QUIZ 25 Q6).

questions.title: Function of simple squamous epithelium
questions.question: Simple squamous epithelium is characterised by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Lining absorptive surfaces along the digestive tract is the role of simple columnar epithelium with microvilli, not simple squamous epithelium.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Protection is chiefly the role of stratified squamous epithelium, which resists friction; simple squamous epithelium is thin, not protective.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Simple squamous epithelium lines moist internal surfaces (vessels, serous cavities, alveoli); it does not have a dry surface -- that is a feature of keratinised skin.
explanations.D: Correct. Simple squamous epithelium is one layer of flat cells with flat nuclei. Being thin it allows exchange of materials (gas exchange in alveoli, filtration in Bowman's capsule), and being smooth it allows easy passage of fluids and easy movement of organs against one another. It takes a different regional name at each site -- endothelium in vessels and the heart, pneumocytes in alveoli, and mesothelium on the pleura, pericardium and peritoneum -- but the smooth-surface function is common to all of them.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: State that simple squamous epithelium provides smooth surfaces, distinguishing this function from absorption and protection.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Provides smooth surfaces" (Quiz 26 Q1). Concept reused from docs/Kasr-Source-Imports/concept/101-ISK-mcq-concepts.md (CON-FND-E51851DAB2DD13); overlay in docs/Assiut-Source-Imports/pending-live/AUN-PMS-102-histology-overlay.md.

questions.title: Cell type lining absorptive membranes
questions.question: Absorptive membranes are lined by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Simple squamous epithelium is suited to exchange and smooth surfaces, not the surface-area-maximising absorption of the intestinal lining.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Ciliated cells move fluid or particles across a surface; motility, not absorption, is their defining function.
explanations.C: Correct. A microvillus is a short finger-like projection whose actin-filament core is inserted into a terminal web; it has no axoneme and does not move, but it increases surface area for absorption. Seen by light microscopy, a carpet of microvilli forms the brush or striated border of the absorptive columnar cell of the intestine. Absorptive membranes such as the intestinal lining are therefore lined by columnar cells bearing this microvillous brush border.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Numerous secretory granules mark a secretory cell, not specifically an absorptive one.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: Identify columnar cells with a microvillous brush border as the cells lining absorptive membranes.

questions.title: Appearance of the superficial layer in stratified squamous epithelium
questions.question: In stratified squamous epithelium:

options.A: The surface layer of cells is always keratinized
options.B: Its basal cells rest on an elastic lamina
options.C: The cells in its most superficial layer are flattened
options.D: It lines the ducts of sweat glands

explanations.A: Incorrect. The keratinised form (epidermis of skin) is only one variant; the non-keratinised form lines the oesophagus, oral cavity, cornea, anal canal, urethral tip and vagina, so the surface is not "always" keratinised.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Its basal cells rest on the basement membrane, not specifically on an "elastic lamina" (a term more associated with blood vessel walls).
explanations.C: Correct. Stratified squamous epithelium is named for the shape of its superficial cells: a basal layer of columnar cells with basal oval nuclei, intermediate polyhedral cells joined by desmosomes, and a superficial layer of flat cells with flat nuclei. It is 5-30 layers thick and functions in protection against friction. Classification of a stratified epithelium is always read from this superficial layer, even when its basal cells are a different shape (columnar), which is why it is still called "stratified squamous."
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sweat gland ducts are lined by stratified cuboidal epithelium, not stratified squamous.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: State that stratified squamous epithelium is classified by its flattened superficial layer, distinguishing this from its (columnar) basal cell shape.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: The cells in its most superficial layer are flattened" (Quiz 26 Q4). Concept reused from docs/Kasr-Source-Imports/concept/101-ISK-mcq-concepts.md (CON-FND-8FEBD5195DCED2); overlay in docs/Assiut-Source-Imports/pending-live/AUN-PMS-102-histology-overlay.md.

questions.title: Epithelial lining of the pleura
questions.question: The pleura is lined with:

explanations.A: Correct. Simple squamous epithelium takes a different regional name at each site: endothelium lining blood vessels and the heart, pneumocytes lining lung alveoli, and mesothelium lining the serous membranes -- the pleura, pericardium and peritoneum. Being smooth, this single layer of flat cells allows the easy movement of the lung against the chest wall with each breath. The pleura is therefore lined by simple squamous epithelium under the regional name mesothelium.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Simple columnar epithelium lines absorptive/secretory surfaces such as the gut, not the smooth-gliding serous pleura.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Stratified squamous epithelium is a friction-resistant lining (skin, oesophagus), not the thin, smooth mesothelial lining of the pleura.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Pseudostratified columnar ciliated epithelium lines the respiratory tract's conducting airways (trachea, bronchi), not the pleural surface.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: State that the pleura is lined by simple squamous epithelium (mesothelium).

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Simple squamous epithelium" (Quiz 26 Q5). questions.title: Example of a simple tubular gland
questions.question: An example of a simple tubular gland is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Merocrine names a mode of secretion (exocytosis with no cell loss), not a gland shape/architecture category.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The salivary glands are compound tubulo-alveolar glands, not simple tubular ones.
explanations.C: Correct. The combined classification of exocrine glands runs simple tubular, simple branched tubular, simple coiled tubular, compound tubular, simple alveolar, simple branched alveolar, compound alveolar, and simple/simple branched/compound tubulo-alveolar. Examples in each form include the intestinal glands (crypts) as simple tubular, the fundic glands of the stomach as simple branched tubular, the sweat gland as simple coiled tubular, the sebaceous gland as simple branched alveolar, and the salivary glands as compound tubulo-alveolar. The intestinal glands are the standard example of the simple tubular form specifically.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Goblet cells are unicellular mucous glands, not a multicellular gland with a tubular architecture.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: Identify the intestinal glands as an example of a simple tubular gland in the combined exocrine gland classification.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Intestinal glands" (Quiz 27 Q1). Concept reused from docs/Kasr-Source-Imports/concept/101-ISK-mcq-concepts.md (CON-FND-677595D34287F6); overlay in docs/Assiut-Source-Imports/pending-live/AUN-PMS-102-histology-overlay.md.

questions.title: Glandular epithelium secreting directly into the blood
questions.question: The glandular epithelium that secretes directly into the blood stream is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Merocrine names a mode of exocrine secretion (exocytosis), not the duct-absent endocrine category that secretes into blood.
explanations.B: Correct. Glands are classified by the presence or absence of a duct: an exocrine gland has ducts carrying its secretion to a surface, while an endocrine gland is ductless -- groups of secretory cells with blood capillaries between them, whose hormone is carried away by the blood to distant parts of the body. This ductless, blood-borne route is exactly what distinguishes an endocrine gland. A mixed gland (e.g. the pancreas) has both an exocrine part with ducts and an endocrine part without.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Holocrine names a mode of exocrine secretion (whole-cell rupture, as in sebaceous glands), not the endocrine (ductless, blood-borne) category.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Exocrine glands secrete via a duct to a surface, the opposite of the ductless, blood-borne route that defines endocrine secretion.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: Identify endocrine glands as ductless glands secreting directly into the bloodstream.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Endocrine" (Quiz 27 Q2). Concept reused from docs/Kasr-Source-Imports/concept/101-ISK-mcq-concepts.md (CON-FND-0A988681FF1ABF); overlay in docs/Assiut-Source-Imports/pending-live/AUN-PMS-102-histology-overlay.md.

questions.title: Mode of secretion of merocrine glands
questions.question: Merocrine glands:

options.C: Lose their cells during the process of secretion
options.D: Lose their apices during the process of secretion

explanations.A: Incorrect. Merocrine is a mode of exocrine (ducted) secretion, not a ductless (endocrine) category.
explanations.B: Correct. By mode of secretion an exocrine gland is merocrine, apocrine or holocrine. Merocrine secretion is discharged outside the cell by exocytosis with no change to the secretory cell -- it is the commonest mode, and the salivary glands are the example. This contrasts with apocrine secretion (loses part of the apical cytoplasm, e.g. lactating mammary gland) and holocrine secretion (the whole cell ruptures and is lost, e.g. sebaceous gland).
explanations.C: Incorrect. Losing the whole cell during secretion describes holocrine secretion (e.g. sebaceous gland), not merocrine.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Losing part of the apex during secretion describes apocrine secretion (e.g. lactating mammary gland), not merocrine.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: State that merocrine glands discharge their secretion by exocytosis with no loss of cell substance.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Discharge their secretion by exocytosis" (Quiz 27 Q3). questions.title: Function of myoepithelial cells
questions.question: Functions of the myoepithelial cells include:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Active ion transport is a function of specialised transporting epithelial cells, not the contractile myoepithelial cell.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Modification of secreted proteins occurs in the Golgi apparatus of secretory cells, not in myoepithelial cells.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Excitability is a defining property of nerve and muscle cells generally; it is not the specific function tested here for myoepithelial cells.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Molecular filtering is a basement membrane function, not a myoepithelial cell function.
explanations.E: Correct. Myo-epithelium is a special type of epithelium modified to contract. Its cells lie basally, between the base of the secretory cells and their basement membrane, and when they contract they squeeze the secretory cells so that secretion is discharged into the ducts. They are found around the acini of the salivary glands, mammary glands and sweat glands, and contractility is their defining function.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: State that contractility is the defining function of myoepithelial cells.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Contractility" (Quiz 27 Q4). Concept reused from docs/Kasr-Source-Imports/concept/101-ISK-mcq-concepts.md (CON-FND-38ABCC4E4E4E68); overlay in docs/Assiut-Source-Imports/pending-live/AUN-PMS-102-histology-overlay.md.

questions.title: Criterion used to classify covering and lining epithelia
questions.question: Which of the following cellular features is used in naming types of covering and lining epithelia?

options.A: Shape of cells in the basal layer
options.B: Nature of the cell junctions that are present

explanations.A: Incorrect. Naming reads from the superficial layer's shape in a stratified epithelium (not the basal layer), so basal-layer shape alone is not the classification criterion.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The type and distribution of cell junctions is a separate structural feature, not the primary criterion used to name a covering/lining epithelium.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Nuclear size follows cell shape as a secondary clue, but it is not itself the primary naming criterion.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Every epithelium rests on a basement membrane (of which the basal lamina is a component), so its mere presence cannot distinguish one epithelial type from another.
explanations.E: Correct. Surface epithelium is classified first by the number of layers -- simple (one layer, every cell on the basement membrane) versus stratified (more than one layer) -- and then by cell shape: a simple epithelium is subdivided by the shape of all its cells, a stratified epithelium by the shape of its superficial cells only. The nucleus takes the shape of the cell that holds it, so naming the nuclear shape is a second way of asking for cell shape. This two-step scheme (layers, then shape) is the standard classification of covering and lining epithelia.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: State that surface epithelium is classified first by the number of cell layers, then by cell shape.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Number of cell layers" (Quiz 27 Q5). Concept reused from docs/Kasr-Source-Imports/concept/101-ISK-mcq-concepts.md (CON-FND-28D12B544C3BA3); overlay in docs/Assiut-Source-Imports/pending-live/AUN-PMS-102-histology-overlay.md.

questions.title: Mode of secretion releasing sebum
questions.question: Which of the following is CORRECT for the release of sebum?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Eccrine describes merocrine-type sweat gland secretion (exocytosis, no cell loss), not the sebaceous gland's mode.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Exocytosis with no cell loss describes merocrine secretion, not the whole-cell-loss mode that releases sebum.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Apocrine secretion loses only part of the apical cytoplasm (e.g. lactating mammary gland); sebum release loses the whole cell, going further than apocrine.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Merocrine secretion (e.g. salivary glands) involves no loss of cell substance, unlike sebum release.
explanations.E: Correct. In holocrine secretion the product accumulates inside the cell, the swollen cell ruptures, and the whole cell is lost along with the secretion; the sebaceous gland releasing sebum is the standard example of this mode. This is the most destructive of the three secretory modes to the cell itself, distinguishing it from merocrine (no cell loss) and apocrine (partial apical loss).

questions.subject: fnd
questions.learning_objective: State that sebum is released by holocrine secretion, in which the whole secretory cell ruptures and is lost.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Holocrine" (Quiz 27 Q6). Concept reused from docs/Kasr-Source-Imports/concept/101-ISK-mcq-concepts.md (CON-FND-D9E83D81037173); overlay in docs/Assiut-Source-Imports/pending-live/AUN-PMS-102-histology-overlay.md.

questions.title: Vertebral extent of the kidneys
questions.question: The kidneys extend from:

options.A: The level of T11 to the level of L3
options.B: The level of T12 to the level of L3
options.C: The level of T11 to the level of L2
options.D: The level of T12 to the level of L2

explanations.A: Incorrect. The superior limit is T12, not T11.
explanations.B: Correct. The kidneys lie retroperitoneally against the posterior abdominal wall, extending vertically from the level of the twelfth thoracic vertebra (T12) to the level of the third lumbar vertebra (L3). Because the right kidney is displaced slightly inferiorly by the liver above it, it sits about half a vertebral level lower than the left, but T12-L3 describes the overall extent of the pair. This span is a fixed anatomical landmark used for surgical and radiological localisation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Both limits are wrong -- the true span is T12 to L3, not T11 to L2.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The inferior limit is L3, not L2.

questions.subject: renal
questions.learning_objective: State that the kidneys extend from the T12 to the L3 vertebral level.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: From the level of T12 to the level of L3" (Quiz28 Q1).

questions.title: Narrowest part of the male urethra
questions.question: The narrowest part of the male urethra is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The spongy (penile) part is the longest part of the urethra, running through the corpus spongiosum, but not the narrowest.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The prostatic part is wider than the membranous part, running through the substance of the prostate.
explanations.C: Incorrect. "Penile" refers to the same segment as "spongy"; it is not the narrowest part.
explanations.D: Correct. The male urethra has four named parts -- preprostatic (intramural), prostatic, membranous and spongy (penile) -- and the membranous part, the short segment passing through the urogenital diaphragm, is the narrowest of the four. This narrowing is clinically relevant as a common site of urethral injury (e.g. in pelvic fracture) and of resistance during catheterisation.

questions.subject: renal
questions.module_subject: AUN-PMS-102 > Urinary System Anatomy > Ureter and Urethra
questions.learning_objective: Identify the membranous part as the narrowest segment of the male urethra.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Membranous" (Quiz28 Q2).

questions.title: Anterior relation of the right kidney
questions.question: One of the anterior relations of the right kidney is:

explanations.A: Correct. The right kidney's anterior surface is related, from superior to inferior, to the right suprarenal gland, the liver, the second part of the duodenum and the right colic (hepatic) flexure, with the liver forming a large part of this anterior relation. This differs from the left kidney's anterior relations, which instead include the spleen, stomach, pancreas, jejunum and splenic flexure. "The liver" and "the spleen" are therefore not interchangeable answers between the two sides.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The pancreas is an anterior relation of the left kidney, not the right.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The spleen is an anterior relation of the left kidney, not the right.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The descending colon lies adjacent to the left kidney's region, not as a standard anterior relation of the right kidney.

questions.subject: renal
questions.learning_objective: Identify the liver as an anterior relation of the right kidney specifically.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: the liver" (Quiz28 Q3).

questions.title: Urethral part surrounded by the internal urethral sphincter
questions.question: The part of the male urethra surrounded by the internal urethral sphincter is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The spongy part is the most distal segment, far from the bladder neck where the internal sphincter sits.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The prostatic part lies distal to the internal sphincter, within the prostate.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The membranous part is surrounded by the external (voluntary, skeletal-muscle) urethral sphincter, not the internal one.
explanations.D: Correct. The most proximal part of the male urethra, the intramural (preprostatic) part, passes through the bladder wall and is surrounded by the internal urethral sphincter, a smooth-muscle sphincter under autonomic control that prevents retrograde ejaculation and involuntary leakage. This is distinct from the external urethral sphincter, a skeletal-muscle sphincter under voluntary control surrounding the membranous part instead.

questions.subject: renal
questions.module_subject: AUN-PMS-102 > Urinary System Anatomy > Ureter and Urethra
questions.learning_objective: Identify the intramural (preprostatic) part as the segment surrounded by the internal urethral sphincter.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Intramural" (Quiz28 Q4).

questions.title: Continuity of the ureter with the renal pelvis
questions.question: The ureters are:

options.A: Continuous superiorly with the renal pelvis
options.B: Vessels that convey urine from the kidneys to the urethra
options.C: Constricted at two points along their course

explanations.A: Correct. Each ureter is a muscular tube continuous superiorly with the funnel-shaped renal pelvis, which collects urine from the major and minor calyces, and continuous inferiorly with the bladder, which it enters obliquely. This superior continuity with the renal pelvis is the defining anatomical relationship being tested here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The ureter conveys urine from the kidney to the bladder, not to the urethra -- the urethra is downstream of the bladder.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The ureter has three, not two, points of physiological constriction along its course (the pelviureteric junction, the pelvic brim, and where it enters the bladder wall).
explanations.D: Incorrect. The ureter's length is closer to 25-30 cm, not exactly 23 cm.

questions.module_subject: AUN-PMS-102 > Urinary System Anatomy > Ureter and Urethra
questions.learning_objective: State that the ureter is continuous superiorly with the renal pelvis.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: They are continuous superiorly with the renal pelvis" (Quiz28 Q5).

questions.title: Incorrect statement about kidney anatomy: renal pyramid location
questions.question: Regarding the anatomy of the kidney, choose the INCORRECT statement:

options.A: Calyces are structures that funnel urine towards the renal pelvis
options.B: Pyramids lie in the renal cortex
options.C: The renal capsule is a layer of collagenous fibers surrounding the kidney
options.D: The right kidney is lower than the left kidney

explanations.A: Incorrect as an answer -- this statement is true: calyces do funnel urine toward the renal pelvis, so it is not the incorrect statement being asked for.
explanations.B: Correct (this is the incorrect statement). On coronal section the kidney shows an outer cortex and an inner medulla; the renal (Malpighian) pyramids -- cone-shaped, bases toward the cortex, apices projecting into the minor calyces -- lie within the medulla, not the cortex. This is why "pyramids lie in the renal cortex" is false among otherwise-true descriptions of kidney anatomy.
explanations.C: Incorrect as an answer -- this statement is true: the renal capsule is a collagenous fibrous layer surrounding the kidney, so it is not the incorrect statement.
explanations.D: Incorrect as an answer -- this statement is true: the right kidney does sit lower than the left because of the liver above it, so it is not the incorrect statement.

questions.subject: renal
questions.learning_objective: Identify that renal pyramids lie in the medulla, not the cortex, as the false statement among true statements about kidney anatomy.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: Pyramids lie in the renal cortex" ("Quiz for organ systems" Q3, p101). questions.title: True statement about the anatomy of the ovary
questions.question: The true statement regarding the ovary is:

options.A: The cortex is highly vascular, much more than the medulla
options.B: The ovaries are suspended by the suspensory ligament of the ovary from the pelvic wall
options.C: The surface epithelium is called the germinal epithelium because it is the source of germ cells

explanations.A: Incorrect. The medulla, not the cortex, is the more vascular of the two ovarian regions.
explanations.B: Correct. The ovary is suspended from the lateral pelvic wall by the suspensory ligament of the ovary (infundibulopelvic ligament), a peritoneal fold that carries the ovarian vessels, nerves and lymphatics; this is a separate structure from the ovarian ligament proper, which anchors the ovary medially to the uterus. Because this ligament carries the ovary's own vessels, it is deliberately clamped and divided during oophorectomy. This suspensory attachment to the pelvic wall is the true statement among the distractors offered here.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The "germinal" epithelium is a historical name from an earlier, now-rejected belief that it was the source of germ cells; it is not actually where germ cells arise.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The ovary is almond-shaped, not diamond-shaped.

questions.title: True fact about testicular anatomy: the mediastinum testis
questions.question: The true fact regarding the testis is:

options.A: The posterior border of the tunica albuginea is thickened to form the mediastinum testis
options.B: The tunica vaginalis has a parietal and a visceral layer without a cavity in between
options.C: The tunica vasculosa is a dense white fibrous coat covering the testis all around
options.D: The testis is covered by four coats

explanations.A: Correct. The testis is covered by three coats -- tunica vaginalis (outermost, a peritoneal remnant with parietal and visceral layers separated by a cavity), tunica albuginea (a dense white fibrous coat), and tunica vasculosa (innermost, vascular). The tunica albuginea's posterior border is thickened to form the mediastinum testis, a fibrous wedge projecting into the gland that gives off septa dividing it into lobules and through which the rete testis and efferent ductules pass. This thickening is the true fact among the distractors offered here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The tunica vaginalis's parietal and visceral layers are in fact separated by a cavity (the cavity of the tunica vaginalis, whose abnormal fluid accumulation is a hydrocele).
explanations.C: Incorrect. "Dense white fibrous coat" describes the tunica albuginea, not the tunica vasculosa, which is instead the innermost, vascular layer.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The testis has three coats, not four.

questions.learning_objective: State that the mediastinum testis is a thickening of the posterior tunica albuginea.

questions.title: Normal position of the uterus
questions.question: The normal position of the uterus is described as:

explanations.A: Incorrect on its own. Anteversion (the cervix-to-vagina angle) is a genuine normal angulation, but naming it alone omits anteflexion, so it is an incomplete description of normal position.
explanations.B: Incorrect on its own. Anteflexion (the body-to-cervix angle) is a genuine normal angulation, but naming it alone omits anteversion, so it is an incomplete description of normal position.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Retroversion (backward tilt) is the abnormal alternative position, not the normal one.
explanations.D: Correct. The normal uterine position combines two separate angulations: anteversion, the forward angle between the long axis of the cervix and the long axis of the vagina, and anteflexion, the forward angle between the long axis of the uterine body and the long axis of the cervix. The standard descriptive term for the normal position is therefore "anteverted and anteflexed" together, not either angulation named alone. This combined position tips the uterine fundus forward over the bladder.

questions.module_subject: AUN-PMS-102 > Genital System Anatomy > Female Genital Anatomy
questions.learning_objective: State that the normal uterine position is described as anteverted and anteflexed together.

field_notes.keySource: Moodle attempt-review, "The correct answer is: anteverted and anteflexed" (Quiz29 [second occurrence] Q4, p105).

questions.title: Length of the vas deferens
questions.question: The length of the vas deferens is:

explanations.A: Correct. The vas deferens (ductus deferens) is a thick-walled muscular tube roughly 45 cm long, running from the tail of the epididymis, through the spermatic cord and inguinal canal, over the pelvic brim, and down to join the duct of the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct. Its considerable length and thick muscular wall allow peristaltic propulsion of sperm at ejaculation. This distinguishes it from much shorter genital-tract segments such as the epididymis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 10 cm considerably underestimates the vas deferens's true length.
explanations.C: Incorrect. 30 cm is closer than the other distractors but still underestimates the vas deferens's approximately 45 cm length.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 4 cm is far too short and would be more consistent with a short structure such as part of the epididymis, not the vas deferens.
